greek: ἀναστὰς δὲ Λαβαν τὸ πρωὶ κατεφίλησεν τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰς θυγατέρας αὐτοῦ καὶ εὐλόγησεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἀποστραφεὶς Λαβαν ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτοῦ.
hint: In the morning Laban kisses and blesses his sons and daughters and goes back to his place.

notes.text: καταφιλέω, *to kiss tenderly*, which Middle Liddell gives that sense and no other.

greek: Καὶ Ιακωβ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ὁδόν. καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἶδεν παρεμβολὴν θεοῦ παρεμβεβληκυῖαν, καὶ συνήντησαν αὐτῷ οἱ ἄγγελοι τοῦ θεοῦ.
hint: Going on his way, Jacob sees an encampment of God, and God's messengers meet him.

notes.text: παρεμβολή is first *an insertion, interpolation*; *an encampment* is its second sense, and the Hebrew is *maḥăneh*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς, *with his eyes*.

hint: The rest of the gift: milking camels and their young, cows, bulls, asses and foals.

reading: [[camels|camels, the camels in an army, the camelry and camel-brigade|κάμηλος]] [[suckling|suckling, giving suck|θηλάζω]] and [[the young children|the young children, the young slave-lads|παιδίον]] of them thirty, [[bullocks|bullocks and bulls and oxen, cows, oxen, kine and cattle, ox-hide shields|βοῦς]] forty, bulls ten, [[asses|asses, beasts of burden, windlasses and pulleys, upper millstones, beakers and wine-cups|ὄνος]] twenty and [[foals|foals, young horses, colts, fillies, young animals and puppies, young girls and maidens|πῶλος]] ten.

greek: καὶ ἔδωκεν διὰ χειρὸς τοῖς παισὶν αὐτοῦ ποίμνιον κατὰ μόνας. εἶπεν δὲ τοῖς παισὶν αὐτοῦ Προπορεύεσθε ἔμπροσθέν μου καὶ διάστημα ποιεῖτε ἀνὰ μέσον ποίμνης καὶ ποίμνης.
hint: Jacob hands each flock to a servant and sends them ahead with space between flock and flock.

[[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[to the children|to the children, to the sons, to the daughters, to the grandchildren, to the boys and youths and lads, to the girls and maidens, to the slaves and servants and men and maids|παῖς]] of him [[go before|go before, go forward, come forward, be promoted and advance|προπορεύομαι]] [[before|before and in front of|ἔμπροσθεν]] of me and an interval [[make|make, do, produce, create|ποιέω]] [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two|ἀνά + accusative; μέσος]] [[of a flock|of a flock, of a flock of sheep|ποίμνη]] and [[of a flock|of a flock, of a flock of sheep|ποίμνη]].

greek: καὶ ἐνετείλατο τῷ πρώτῳ λέγων Ἐάν σοι συναντήσῃ Ησαυ ὁ ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἐρωτᾷ σε λέγων Τίνος εἶ καὶ ποῦ πορεύῃ, καὶ τίνος ταῦτα τὰ προπορευόμενά σου;
hint: Jacob tells the first servant Esau will ask whose he is, where he is going, and whose the flock is.

notes.text: Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

hint: The servant is to answer that the flock is a gift from Esau's servant Jacob, who follows behind.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Berlin papyrus, 911, begins the verse so; Codex Alexandrinus puts καί before it.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: καὶ ἐνετείλατο τῷ πρώτῳ καὶ τῷ δευτέρῳ καὶ τῷ τρίτῳ καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς προπορευομένοις ὀπίσω τῶν ποιμνίων τούτων λέγων Κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο λαλήσατε Ησαυ ἐν τῷ εὑρεῖν ὑμᾶς αὐτὸν
hint: Jacob gives the second, the third and every drover the same instructions for meeting Esau.

greek: καὶ ἐρεῖτε Ἰδοὺ ὁ παῖς σου Ιακωβ παραγίνεται ὀπίσω ἡμῶν. εἶπεν γάρ Ἐξιλάσομαι τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ἐν τοῖς δώροις τοῖς προπορευομένοις αὐτοῦ, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο ὄψομαι τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ· ἴσως γὰρ προσδέξεται τὸ πρόσωπόν μου.
hint: Jacob plans to appease Esau's face with the gifts going ahead, then see that face; perhaps Esau will accept him.

notes.text: ἐξιλάσκομαι, *to propitiate*, with πρόσωπον: the Hebrew is *ʾăkappĕrâ pānāyw*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take them for a proper name.

[[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] I will propitiate [[the face|the face and visage and countenance, the look, the mask, the outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] of him [[in the gifts|within, inside of, and by means of the gifts, the presents, the votive gifts, the blessings|ἐν; δῶρον]] [[to the things going before|to the things going before, to the things going forward, to the things coming forward, to the things being promoted and advancing|προπορεύομαι]] of him, and [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after|μετά + accusative]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[I will see|I will see, I will perceive, I will behold, I will look at|ὁράω]] [[the face|the face and visage and countenance, the look, the mask, the outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] of him; [[equally|equally and in like manner, fairly and equitably, probably and perhaps, about|ἴσως]] [[for|for, since and as, for otherwise and else, now, but, why and what, would that|γάρ]] [[will receive favourably|will receive favourably and accept, will receive hospitably, will admit into, will admit to citizenship, will admit, will wait for and expect, will wait patiently|προσδέχομαι]] [[the face|the face and visage and countenance, the look, the mask, the outward appearance|πρόσωπον]] of me.

greek: καὶ παρεπορεύοντο τὰ δῶρα κατὰ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, αὐτὸς δὲ ἐκοιμήθη τὴν νύκτα ἐκείνην ἐν τῇ παρεμβολῇ.
hint: The gifts go on ahead, and Jacob spends that night in the encampment.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads προεπορεύοντο, *went on before*.

hint: That night Jacob takes his two wives, two slave-girls and eleven children across the ford of the Jabbok.

notes.text: The Hebrew hears the name Yabbōq in the wrestling of the verses that follow, yēʾābēq.

reading: [[having stood up|having stood up, having risen, having risen to fight against, having risen to go and set out|ἀνίστημι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the night-season|the night-season, the night, the watches of the night, the dark of night, the night of death|νύξ]] [[that|that, the one there, the more remote|ἐκεῖνος]] [[took|took, received, took hold of and grasped and seized|λαμβάνω]] the two [[women|women, mistresses and ladies, wives and spouses, mortal women|γυνή]] and the two [[young girls|young girls and maidens, young slaves and courtesans|παιδίσκη]] and the eleven [[young children|young children, young slave-lads|παιδίον]] of him and [[made a stride|made a stride, walked and stood with the legs apart, stepped across and passed over, crossed over|διαβαίνω]] [[the crossing over|the crossing over and passage, the means and place of crossing, the ford, the bridge|διάβασις]] of the [[name:Ιαβοκ]];

hint: Jacob takes them across the torrent and brings over all he has.

notes.text: No Middle Liddell entry; LSJ's χειμάρροος is *winter-flowing*, and as a noun *torrent*, and in the Septuagint *river*, *valley, watercourse*.

greek: ὑπελείφθη δὲ Ιακωβ μόνος, καὶ ἐπάλαιεν ἄνθρωπος μετʼ αὐτοῦ ἕως πρωί.
hint: Jacob is left alone, and a man wrestles with him until morning.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀπόστειλόν με· ἀνέβη γὰρ ὁ ὄρθρος. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Οὐ μή σε ἀποστείλω, ἐὰν μή με εὐλογήσῃς.
hint: At dawn the man asks to be let go; Jacob refuses without a blessing.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus turns the two about.

hint: The man asks Jacob's name, and he gives it.

notes.text: Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ Οὐ κληθήσεται ἔτι τὸ ὄνομά σου Ιακωβ, ἀλλὰ Ισραηλ ἔσται τὸ ὄνομά σου, ὅτι ἐνίσχυσας μετὰ θεοῦ καὶ μετὰ ἀνθρώπων δυνατός.
hint: Jacob is renamed Israel, as strong with God and powerful with men.

notes.text: The Hebrew hears the name in *śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm*, *he strove with God*, which the Greek gives as ἐνίσχυσας μετὰ θεοῦ.

greek: ἠρώτησεν δὲ Ιακωβ καὶ εἶπεν Ἀνάγγειλόν μοι τὸ ὄνομά σου. καὶ εἶπεν Ἵνα τί τοῦτο ἐρωτᾷς τὸ ὄνομά μου; καὶ ηὐλόγησεν αὐτὸν ἐκεῖ.
hint: Jacob asks the man's name; the man asks why, and blesses him there.

greek: ἀνέτειλεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ ἥλιος, ἡνίκα παρῆλθεν τὸ Εἶδος τοῦ θεοῦ· αὐτὸς δὲ ἐπέσκαζεν τῷ μηρῷ αὐτοῦ.
hint: The sun rises on Jacob as he passes the Form of God, limping on his thigh.

notes.text: No Middle Liddell entry; LSJ's ἐπισκάζω is *limp upon*, and it cites this very verse.

reading: [[made to rise up|made to rise up, made to grow up, gave birth to and brought to light, rose, took its rise, grew|ἀνατέλλω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], to him [[the sun|the sun, the day and a day, Helios the sun-god|ἥλιος]], [[at which time|at which time and when, since, whenever|ἡνίκα]] [[went by|went by, went beside, went past, passed by, passed, outstripped, outwitted and escaped and eluded, arrived at, passed in, went into, passed without heeding, passed over and disregarded and slighted, overstepped and transgressed, passed unnoticed and escaped the notice of, came forward|παρέρχομαι]] the [[name:Εἶδος]] [[of the God|of him who is God definitively, of the one the article marks out, of the known and the only|θεός]]; he [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], was limping upon [[to the thigh|to the thigh, to the leg-bones|μηρός]] of him.

greek: ἕνεκεν τούτου οὐ μὴ φάγωσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ισραηλ τὸ νεῦρον, ὃ ἐνάρκησεν, ὅ ἐστιν ἐπὶ τοῦ πλάτους τοῦ μηροῦ, ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης, ὅτι ἥψατο τοῦ πλάτους τοῦ μηροῦ Ιακωβ τοῦ νεύρου καὶ ἐνάρκησεν.
hint: The sons of Israel still do not eat the sinew that grew numb on the thigh, because of the touch.

notes.text: [[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus adds γάρ.

reading: [[on account of|on account of, for the sake of, because of, for, as far as regards|ἕνεκα]] [[of this|of this, of the nearer, of what follows|οὗτος]] not [[not|not, that not, perhaps, surely not and you don't mean to say that|μή]] [[may eat|may eat, may eat of|ἐσθίω]] the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[the sinew|the sinew and tendon, the tendons of the feet, the sinews and vigour, the gut and cord made of sinew, the cord of a sling|νεῦρον]], which [[grew stiff|grew stiff, grew numb|ναρκάω]], which is [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + genitive]] [[of the breadth|of the breadth and width|πλάτος]] [[of the thigh|of the thigh, of the leg-bones|μηρός]], [[until|until, till, while and so long as|ἕως]] [[of the day|of the day, of the day-break, of the time|ἡμέρα]] [[of this|of this, of the nearer, of what follows|οὗτος]], [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[fastened himself to|fastened himself to, clung to, hung on by, laid hold of, grasped, touched, engaged in and took part in, laid hold of and disputed|ἅπτω]] [[of the breadth|of the breadth and width|πλάτος]] [[of the thigh|of the thigh, of the leg-bones|μηρός]] of [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[of the sinew|of the sinew and tendon, of the tendons of the feet, of the sinews and vigour, of the gut and cord made of sinew, of the cord of a sling|νεῦρον]] and [[grew stiff|grew stiff, grew numb|ναρκάω]].
